items.title: Student Protests Expand to More Than 40 French Cities
items.summary: Union members, parents and teachers joined the demonstrations, broadening the student-led protest movement that has closed hundreds of French high schools since late September.

items.title: UK Security Adviser Jonathan Powell Traveled to Israel Ahead of Consulate Closure
items.summary: Jonathan Powell, Britain’s national security adviser, visited Israel last week to try to negotiate over the looming closure of his country’s consulate in Jerusalem, according to three officials.

items.title: U.S. Sends Reaper Drones to Colombia and Ecuador to Hunt Cartels
items.summary: MQ-9 Reaper drones — known for high-profile deadly strikes — have been shifted from Africa to Colombia and Ecuador, U.S. officials said.

items.title: Live From the Barracks: Three Juntas Launch TV Channel
items.summary: Three African countries have started Tafouk TV, a Russia-partnered broadcast channel, after throwing out Western journalists and cracking down on local media.

items.title: Man Arrested in Connection With Incident at UK Air Base RAF Fairford
items.summary: A 22-year-old from London was the seventh person to be arrested by the counterterrorism police investigating an incident at R.A.F. Fairford last month.

items.title: Spain Cancels Arrest Warrant for Carles Puigdemont, Catalan Separatist Leader
items.summary: The Spanish Supreme Court canceled an arrest warrant for Carles Puigdemont, who has been living in self-imposed exile in Belgium.

items.title: Kenya Records Ebola Case for First Time
items.summary: The authorities said that the virus had been diagnosed in a man arriving from the Democratic Republic of Congo and that they were taking measures to prevent any spread.

items.title: Drones Hit Ships Off Bulgaria’s Black Sea Coast, Prime Minister Says
items.summary: A rescue effort was underway, Prime Minister Rumen Radev said, after one of the two ships sank. It was not immediately clear where the drones originated.

items.title: German Officials Arrest Former Spy Chief on Espionage Charges
items.summary: August Hanning is accused of helping foreign governments. His arrest shook the German political world and had roots in a steakhouse-heiress kidnapping plot.

items.title: India Cut 130 Million From Voter Roll, Fueling Protests Against Modi
items.summary: Public anger is growing over an exercise that critics say undermines the world’s largest democracy, particularly disenfranchising Muslims under the Hindu nationalist government.

items.title: Europe’s Trade Tensions With China Are Coming to a Head
items.summary: The European Union is weighing tougher trade measures as negotiators prepare to meet Chinese officials in Beijing, with surging exports from China pressuring key industries in Europe.

items.title: China’s ‘Self-Reliance’ Drive Is Upending Trade With Europe
items.summary: China’s push to manufacture more at home has widened its trade imbalance with Europe, intensifying pressure on European industries and policymakers to take action.

items.title: Airfares Have Spiked. Is the Death of Spirit Airlines to Blame?
items.summary: In the wake of the ultra-low-cost carrier’s closure, and with the cost of fuel and labor rising, domestic fares have become less competitive. But there are ways to parry higher prices.

items.title: Inheritances Can Shatter Families. Could a Therapist Help?
items.summary: As the country faces the greatest wealth transfer in history, some people are turning to therapists to help them pass on their assets in a way that preserves harmony.

items.title: Need Help Paying for College? Try Bass Fishing.
items.summary: The popularity of competitive bass fishing has inspired a growing number of youth, high school and college fishing programs.

items.title: Porsche, Facing Falling Profits, Plans to Cut 25% of Its Work Force
items.summary: The German sports car maker once thrived in China and powered profits for its parent company, Volkswagen. Now it hopes to do more with less.

items.title: S&P 500 Hits Record High Amid Rising Interest Rates and Elevated Oil Prices
items.summary: The S&P 500 rose 0.6 percent on Tuesday, exceeding its previous peak set in August and taking its gain this year to more than 14 percent.

items.title: How Trump’s Tariff War With Canada Ensnared the Can-Am Spyder
items.summary: The Can-Am Spyder has a devoted fan base across the United States. Now it’s a casualty in the trade war with Canada.

items.title: Emmy Awards Move to Prime Video in Six-Year Deal With Amazon
items.summary: The Television Academy is moving its awards telecast to streaming, following the lead of the Oscars.

items.title: Paramount Closes Merger With Warner Bros. Discovery to Form Skydance
items.summary: After a legal battle, the two Hollywood giants have become one. But the new company is saddled with debt, and in a memo to employees, its leaders hinted at cost cuts.

items.title: Inside Binance Founder Changpeng Zhao’s Life After Prison
items.summary: Changpeng Zhao, jailed in the United States for a financial crime and pardoned by President Trump, is now living a gilded life in the United Arab Emirates.

items.title: Who’s to Blame When A.I. Goes Rogue?
items.summary: Many think artificial intelligence companies should be held liable for their runaway technology. But legal scholars say applying existing law could be messy.

items.title: OpenAI’s Greg Brockman Backs Out of Second $25 Million Donation to A.I. Super PAC
items.summary: Greg Brockman, OpenAI’s president and co-founder, said internally that the super PAC, Leading the Future, had become a “distraction” for the A.I. company.

items.title: How Meta Uses A.I. Data Centers to Avoid Billions in Federal Taxes
items.summary: Meta is exploiting a lucrative tax break intended to support research and experimentation. Its own accountants say the gambit is risky.

items.title: Why My Conversations with OpenAI’s ‘ChatGPT for Teens’ Made Me Very Worried
items.summary: A new mode includes a study tool, but it still does a user’s homework. And a children’s safety nonprofit says the chatbot flunked its tests.

items.title: Energy Firms Try to Squeeze More Power Out of Old Nuclear Plants
items.summary: It takes a long time to build new nuclear plants. So, some U.S. companies are looking to get more electricity out of reactors that already exist.

items.title: In Race With U.S., China Struggles to Recruit Foreign A.I. Researchers
items.summary: China’s booming artificial intelligence sector has given local researchers good reason to remain in the country, but it has yet to lure overseas scientists despite a government push.

items.title: Gears of War: E-Day Is Nostalgic With Rich Visuals
items.summary: In Gears of War: E-Day, it’s fun to see the origins of beloved characters in grand scale, even if its play feels conservative.

items.title: South Korea Investigates Possible Use of A.I. in Hackings on Its Banks
items.summary: The president said there were signs that such models were used in recent attacks on several banks involving customer data. Police are investigating.

items.title: Mixed Human Feelings After a Day at a Park Full of Robots
items.summary: I went to Galaxy Robot Park in Seoul to see how we might one day live with robots. It was part cutting-edge technology, part theatrics.
